Hi Sophie & Alan,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great call. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can make the technical deep-dive efficient: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- LexiSearch wants to improve search relevance for product docs and support articles using an embeddings + reranker pipeline.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms tail latency for served results, support for structured output/tool calling for answer blocks, and strict data residency for PII-containing docs (US region).
- Success metrics: Precision@10 and NDCG@10 improvements vs current baseline, with guardrails around latency and token cost.

Immediate asks / questions for your engineering team (so Rafael can prepare):
1) Auth & infra: Are you planning to use our Hosted API (API key) or Private deployment (mTLS/KMS)? Any constraints on inbound IPs or VPC peering we should know about?
2) Routing & topology: Will you route requests through a central API gateway or call Redwood directly from your search service? Any preference for region-level routing?
3) Integration shape: Do you want a two-stage pipeline (embed -> candidate retrieval -> rerank) or an end-to-end ranking call (single API that accepts candidate doc ids + query)?
4) Evaluation data: Can you share a ~500-query eval set (queries + ground-truth doc ids or relevance labels)? We can run initial MRR/NDCG evals.

What we'll deliver before the next call:
- A short integration guide for the reranker flow (attached) and a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones.
- Rafael will include a suggested SDK snippet and recommended top_k defaults for initial testing.

Attachments: redwood_reranker_integration_guide.pdf (PDF, 320KB), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

Proposed next step: technical deep-dive next week - Rafael + Alan to pair on architecture + ops. What time windows work for you?

Thanks,

Hey Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

1) Auth & infra: We prefer Hosted API for initial PoC (API key), but we will need the option to migrate to a Private deployment later. For the PoC we cannot expose full-text docs outside our corp network - we'll provide a sanitized eval set first.
2) Routing: We plan to call Redwood directly from our search service (Golang microservice). Low-latency region = us-west.
3) Integration: We want to start with a two-stage pipeline (embed -> retriever -> reranker) so we can re-use our existing ANN index (we use Faiss).
4) Eval data: We can share a 600-query eval set (sanitized) by EOD Monday.

Questions for Rafael:
- For the reranker call, what's the recommended candidate pool size you suggest to pass in? We have ~10M docs; retrieving 200 candidates is possible but we want guidance on top_k tuning vs latency/cost.
- What metrics should we compute locally vs ask Redwood to return (e.g., should we compute NDCG on our side from scores you return, or ask for per-document relevance scores)?

We're available Tue/Wed next week for the technical deep-dive (AM Pacific preferred).

Hi Sophie / Alan - Rafael here (Solutions Engineer). Great questions - below are concrete recommendations and a proposed evaluation plan.

High-level recommended integration (PoC):
- Step 1 (Embedding): Call Redwood embeddings API to vectorize query. Store document vectors in your FAISS index as you already do.
- Step 2 (Retrieval): Retrieve candidate doc ids from FAISS. Initial candidate pool: top_k_retriever = 200.
- Step 3 (Rerank): Call Redwood Reranker API with the query and candidate doc snippets (we recommend <= 512 tokens per candidate). Use reranker_top_k = 50 for the first pass to balance latency/cost.
- Step 4 (Serve): Return top 10 results to UI. Optionally use Redwood streaming + structured output to generate an answer block for the top result and include source attribution.

Why these defaults?
- Retriever big-K (200) increases recall so the reranker has good candidates.
- Passing 50 candidates to the model (reranker_top_k=50) is a pragmatic balance: on our infra we see per-request latency in the 80-180ms range depending on sequence lengths and batching.

API/SDK details (quick snippet & auth models):
- Hosted: API key header (Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>). Rate limits depend on plan; we can bump for PoC.
- Private: mTLS + KMS integration for keys; supports VPC peering.
- SDK: We have official SDKs (Python/Go/Node). Example pseudo-call for rerank: 

// pseudo-code (Python)
# embeddings -> FAISS retrieval -> rerank
query_vec = redwood.embeddings.create("text-embed-001", text=query)
candidates = faiss.search(query_vec, k=200)
resp = redwood.rerank.create(
    model="rerank-1.0",
    query=query,
    candidates=[{"id": c.id, "snippet": c.snippet} for c in candidates[:50]],
    return_scores=True,
    explain_tokens=False
)

Key rerank params to tune:
- candidates_passed (K_ret -> initial retrieval size)
- reranker_top_k (K_rerank -> how many candidates you send to model)
- return_scores (boolean) to get model scores for computing NDCG/MRR locally
- explain_tokens (boolean) if you want token-level attributions (adds latency/cost)

Evaluation & relevance metrics
- Compute: Precision@k (k=1,3,10), Recall@k, MRR, NDCG@k (k=10). For significance testing use paired t-test or bootstrap on query-level metrics.
- Suggested process: run baseline retrieval-only (your current FAISS + sparse signals) vs embeddings+reranker. Use human-annotated judgments where possible.
- If you want Redwood to help: send us the eval set and we can run MRR/NDCG comparisons and provide a short report (we'll keep data per the MAP).

Operational notes
- Cost: Passing 50 candidates to the reranker increases token consumption - we can run a quick cost estimate once we have average snippet lengths.
- Latency: If you need <100ms p95, we can explore quantized model variants and batching strategies - also consider a hybrid flow that serves top-3 from cache + reranker for freshness.

Next steps (proposed):
- Sophie: share sanitized eval set by EOD Mon (you mentioned 600 queries) - Rafael to run initial comparisons.
- Marissa/Neha: confirm PoC timeline in the MAP (I updated attached MAP with estimator rows).
- Schedule: Rafael + Alan technical deep-dive Tue 06/09 AM Pacific. I'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: SOW_draft_v1.docx (Word, 85KB)

Let me know if you want a sample output format for the reranker API (we can include a JSON schema for structured output + attribution).
